events.title: Géza and Ladislaus defeat King Solomon of Hungary at Mogyoród
events.description: Dukes Géza and Ladislaus, claiming the throne, defeated their cousin King Solomon of Hungary at Mogyoród and forced him to flee to the kingdom's western borderland. Géza was proclaimed king that year, but Solomon kept the western regions.

events.title: A palace revolt in Granada deposes Muhammad III
events.description: On Eid al-Fitr the citizens of Granada stormed palaces in the city, deposed the Nasrid emir Muhammad III and placed his brother Nasr on the throne. Muhammad's capture of Ceuta had provoked an alliance of Castile, Aragon and the Marinids against Granada.

events.title: Admiral John Byng executed by firing squad
events.description: Convicted of failing to do his utmost to relieve Minorca, Byng was shot on the deck of HMS Monarch at Portsmouth. Voltaire mocked the English for killing an admiral 'to encourage the others'.

events.title: Eli Whitney patents the cotton gin
events.description: Whitney's machine separated cotton fibre from seeds far faster than by hand. It made short-staple cotton highly profitable and fuelled a vast expansion of slavery in the American South.

events.title: Albert Einstein is born in Ulm
events.description: Einstein's theories of special and general relativity transformed ideas of space, time and gravity. He won the 1921 Nobel Prize for explaining the photoelectric effect.
events.html: Einstein's theories of special and general relativity transformed ideas of space, time and gravity. He won the 1921 Nobel Prize for explaining the photoelectric effect.

events.title: Gold Standard Act puts the dollar on gold
events.description: President McKinley signed the act fixing the dollar's value in gold and ending the long political fight over free silver. The US left the gold standard domestically in 1933.
events.html: President McKinley signed the act fixing the dollar's value in gold and ending the long political fight over free silver. The US left the gold standard domestically in 1933.

events.title: Penicillin saves its first American patient
events.description: Anne Miller, dying of streptococcal blood poisoning after a miscarriage, was treated at a New Haven hospital with a scarce supply of penicillin. She recovered and lived to the age of 90.

events.title: Jack Ruby convicted of murdering Lee Harvey Oswald
events.description: A Dallas jury found the nightclub owner guilty of shooting Kennedy's accused assassin on live television and sentenced him to death. The verdict was overturned, and Ruby died before a retrial.
